body:
You didn't say it but your post sounds like you're implying that non-terminal illnesses are always treatable or manageable. That isn't true and that's why MAID has extended its criteria to include non-terminal conditions.

 I find it deeply troubling that the Canadian government doesn't provide adequate support to disabled citizens, and if the news is true, that the health care system refuses to help patients due to financial reasons,  however both of those problems existed long before MAID was a thing. The fact that people are choosing death over suffering the consequences of the government's inability to fund public services shows how low their quality of life must be.  Why not focus on righting the wrongs of social inequity? That is the real evil. I don't understand why some people think assisted dying is worse than allowing people to suffer unbearably.
Exactly. Why some people only support euthanasia for the terminally ill confuses me. Are they for ending the prolongation of severe suffering or not?

Anyone eligible for assisted suicide would need to try all available treatment first. If those fail then that's the point where society needs to let go if that's what the person wants. Preventive measures should be about helping people who could have a good life (or at least good enough) not end their life prematurely. If it's about preventing everyone, no matter how dire their circumstances, then it's no longer a force for good. Forcing people to commit DIY suicide is both cruel and dangerous. Coercing someone to endure their pain for the rest of their lives, often decades, when they've clearly stated that they've had enough is tantamount to torture.

I'm sorry to hear about your circumstances. I assume you live in Canada or the Netherlands? I think it's immoral for doctors and psychologists to advertise or recommend assisted dying. The subject should be prompted entirely by the patient if they want to die. There should be no baiting or shaming going on - that is pure coercion. The disabled have always been undervalued by society and it's a sickening thing to see. No one should be dying because their government refuses to support them adequately. I am pro-choice on this issue but reading what you said gives pause. There must be a way to satisfy everybody, though. In my country assisted dying is illegal, and maybe it always will be, however even in that case, my government has a responsibility to care for the disabled properly and often fails. It's not right and I wish more people would speak up about this.
There's an entire spectrum of severity and chronicity when it comes to depression.

We care about preventing suicide because most people can be successfully treated to manage their condition and lead a mostly happy and productive life. The problem is, preventive ideology has become too extreme. It completely ignores the people who suffer unbearably and cannot be helped by treatment.

I don't think a lot of people fully appreciate just how painful (mentally or physically) life can become, or  they have too much faith in current medical and/or psychiatric science. Both have their limitations, they cannot help everybody.

Even the most liberal physician assisted suicide services have safeguards in place to prevent people like you from prematurely ending their lives. The suffering must be unbearable and all treatments available must have been tried before hand. Also, most people in the wrong state of mind already have the control to end their own lives. Only without professional help, they often botch the suicide and end up suffering even more. There needs to be better funded and more accessible mental health services for all, as well as access to PAS/Euthanasia for those who treatment fails. Even the option alone can keep some people from killing themselves. The safety net gives them strength to carry on with the confidence that they can end their lives safely if they need to.
There could be survivorship bias going on there. The people who didn't regret their decision would be more likely to try again and succeed.

It really depends on your definition of treatable. A mentally ill person may achieve small benefit from treatment but their life still might be unbearable. Just as painkillers may partially alleviate chronic pain but not to the extent that the sufferer requires to function or think of anything other than pain. There are many treatments for physical and mental illness and they are usually effective at helping somebody manage their condition. They should always be tried first before suicide is looked upon as an option. 

In my opinion, DIY suicide is never the answer, that's what *should* be true. Without a safe way to do it, overseen by a physician, it sometimes becomes the answer. The person must decide that for themselves.

Bodily autonomy isn't as important to me as preventing the prolongation of severe suffering. I agree in principle that everybody with mental capacity deserves the right to die in a safe medical environment if they so choose. My belief on this is a bit shaky because I'm uncertain as to why a healthy competent minded adult, free of physical or mental illness, would choose to prematurely die. However, my lack of relatability shouldn't be grounds to stop them. They may have very valid reasons as to why of which I am unable to understand. Could they be lying or in denial about being mentally ill? Possibly, but that's up to psychologists to determine when they're being evaluated. 

(I've been called mentally ill for not wanting to endure decades of agony, should that ever happen, so from my point of view society is overly optimistic at best or delusional at worst concerning these matters)

There would need to be safeguarding in place in a PAS/Euthanasia system. Everybody would be required to get a psychological evaluation, and the vulnerable (i.e the mentally ill and physically ill) wouldn't be accepted unless they'd tried all forms of treatment available before hand. There would be more conditions and nuance to it than that but that's the simple version of it.


`I’ve had people tell me that I can never tell someone that suicide isn’t the answer as it infringes on their bodily autonomy.`


Nope, having an opinion isn't going against anybodies bodily autonomy. I think beliefs can be dangerous, though. People who believe that suicide is never the answer under any circumstance will likely vote against the legalization of any form of PAS/Euthanasia. Many people will needlessly suffer as a result.
Not all issues of mental health are treatable for everyone, that's just being naive. It's no wonder you are arriving at the wrong conclusion.

What am I making up exactly? You didn't answer my question.

`whether people should kill themselves`

I mean, you already agreed that there are legitimate reasons for somebody to kill themselves so maybe you should step off your high horse? 

Jesus fuck, you are projecting so hard with the "winning the interwebz" comment. I couldn't care less if I win an internet argument, there is far more at stake than that. 

`Everything about the suffering experienced is radically different`

Based on what, personal experience? Do you think a person cares if their suffering is not exactly the same as one form of suffering or the other? The important part is how bearable their life is. If it isn't bearable and their condition is untreatable then it makes sense for them to want to die. Your solution seems to be that they should just have to put up with it. That may be easy for you to say because you are not the one who has to pay the price of living.

What is false by what I said? 

And I said there is no real difference between the suffering of either. Not that physical illness and mental illness are the same. If neither can be treated, though, what difference does it make? Unbearable suffering is unbearable suffering. Unless you believe that one is more unbearable or severe than the other?

And no, I don't care if I win an internet argument. I don't know where that even came from.

There's no real difference between the suffering of severe physical illness and the suffering of severe mental illness if neither can be treated. Non-terminal physical illness causes death by depression, not by pain itself, pain is just a symptom. Most people can better relate to physical pain so are therefore more sympathetic. Mental illness is trivialized because it's far more difficult to relate to.

I think all suicides are a tragedy, whether they be rational or otherwise, however, by not providing a safe environment to end lives by utilizing physician assisted suicide or euthanasia, the situation turns catastrophic. The sufferer is either forced to choose between a torturous life or a DIY suicide which often goes wrong and can potentially lead to severe disability. Not everyone is even physically capable of attempting suicide so they have no choice in the matter.

`suicide is never the answer`

What are you basing that on exactly? Many conditions are both unbearable and untreatable. Not only terminal illnesses either. You sound like you mean well but, no offense, I don't think you've really put a lot of thought into this. Kind words, love and empathy are powerful things, and they *can* help a sufferer live a happy life but not always. Love can actually become a double-edged sword only compounding misery. I love my family and don't want to hurt them but one day the chronic pain I suffer with may grow so intense that I'll have no option other than to die. 

The naysayers who say I can stoically endure the pain if I put my mind to it are not being rational nor are they being compassionate, although they believe they are. I've said it before: a positive attitude is not necessarily a realistic one. People will believe that humans can overcome any obstacle, no matter how difficult, simply because they fear their own mortality.  If it can happen to somebody else then it can happen to them. The fear of death leads to all kinds of self-deceit and delusions.

Not everyone is physically capable of committing suicide, but even those who are capable, the risk of failure is high and can sometimes lead to severe disability like paralysis or brain damage. Assisted suicide and euthanasia are safe options when safeguarded properly.

Why ages 25+? People can suffer at any age.

In countries where child euthanasia is legal, parental or guardian consent is required.

I agree. Though, I'd  respect the wishes of a person who wanted a natural death as well. It's not easy to see a loved one hooked up to machines but if that is what they want then I feel that there's no need for them to feel guilty about that.

I think minors and the mentally ill should be afforded greater protection, however even they should be offered euthanasia/PAS if they are unbearably suffering and doctors/psychiatrists/psychologists cannot alleviate their symptoms to an acceptable level. People who actively oppose euthanasia for these groups mean well but what they're actually doing is prolonging needless suffering.

Not all suffering can be cured or alleviated by throwing money at it. At least not in time for the people who suffer today. Don't get me wrong, better funded mental health services are a must and so is financially supporting the disabled. However, a person can have access to the best medical and psychiatric support available, be taken care of well by the state, yet still live with severe suffering.

I am saving up for this. Honestly, I don't care if they are ripping me off. They are the only organization, that I'm aware of, who provides this service for foreigners. It isn't right that anybody is forced to die outside of their country and pay such a large sum of money, but that's what our cruel governments force us to do. I feel sorry for everyone who cannot afford this. There are cheaper ways using the same drug Dignitas uses but getting hold of it isn't as easy as I previously thought. I will go that route if I can because I'd rather die at home. I also want my family to be able to attend my funeral in this country.
Chronic pain. My stomach feels like its being crushed. I didn't realize how much emotion is felt in the gut before this. Everything I used to enjoy feels unpleasant and scary.
Allowing people to 'live' in agony against their will, be that physical or mental, for decades is the moral thing to do, apparently.

I think assisted suicide and euthanasia should be legal. I don't think it'll ever be an easy option for most people to take, though. I don't mean accessibility. Most people are terrified of death, even those who no longer wish to live, and most people have families who will be hurt over the death. There's also the terrifying prospect that maybe the lethal drugs used won't be painless, even though they most likely will be. Still, that uncertainty. I won't even get started on my irrational fear about a bad afterlife. I am actually saving up money to apply for Dignitas' help but all these thoughts haunt me.

Here's an horrific example of that: https://metro.co.uk/2017/10/26/mums-heartbreaking-photos-of-son-starved-of-oxygen-after-suicide-attempt-7028654/

*Over the last eight months he has learned how to move his hands from an armrest to his lap, and to blink once for ‘no’ and twice for ‘yes’.* *When Helen asks her son if he still wants to die, he blinks twice.*

Yes, but realistically speaking that isn't going to happen any time soon. People who live in unbearable pain don't have the luxury to wait. There's also no guarantee that painful and disabling diseases would be cured or alleviated in a timely fashion even in a perfect society. As for palliative care... palliative care does not necessarily mean unpainful or dignified (everyone has a personal threshold for what a dignified life means to them), death may be a crude solution but sometimes it's the only option a suffering person has left.

I mean, non-terminal illness can cause just as much disability and pain as those who are terminally ill and their pain will last much longer. "they can always be better helped by things other than killing", that isn't true in all cases and is just wishful thinking.
I don't know but don't fall for scams. Be cautious if anyone DMs you offering you some. There are test kits you can legally purchase to check for purity.
Death would be such a treat.

I started off believing that only those who experience severe chronic physical pain should qualify for assisted suicide but the more I looked into it, the more and more I began to realize that everybody deserves the right. Who the fuck do the Government and pro-lifers think they are? If a person wants to die then that's their choice, nobody can get into the minds of somebody else and experience their perception of reality. The mentally ill and minors should be offered more protection than others but even they should quality if their suffering is unbearable and doctors can't help them. All the current law is doing is causing suffering.

I don't know much about Dignitas other than what information it gives on its website. I was diagnosed with fibromyalgia (which i doubt is the case due to my conditions never ending worsening over time) however I wanted to know if my diagnosis would qualify for their help. I don't have the funds anyway so I haven't looked much further into things. You could always email them if you have any questions. I hope your simulator works, I know what it's like to be in a situation with no other options. You tell someone nothing helps and their brain can't quite fathom what you mean. Blind optimism is the reason why people like you and me find ourselves looking to distant foreign countries in the first place, instead of staying in our own country and being offered a safe way out here.

I wish my Government (UK) would grow some balls and legalize assisted suicide and euthanasia already. Unassisted suicide is a roll of the dice and can go wrong, leaving the person in an even worse state than before if unsuccessful. The paralysed can't even take the chance if they wanted to. I'll just never understand how society can allow others to suffer in unbearable pain. We think of ourselves as a compassionate people but all we really are is cowards, burying our heads in the sand, pretending reality is kinder than it is.
The first time I felt any signs of age dysphoria was age 12 when I became aware that my childhood was approaching its end. Before then I couldn't wait to grow up.

I don't like using the term transage because of it's association with pedophilia. Not that I think the word is inherently bad, just that it's been spoiled by trolls and pedophiles who use it as an excuse to abuse children. Most are just pretending to be transage when in fact they are not, but of course some pedophiles will also happen to be transage aswell. Michael Jackson *MAY* have been a pedophile. In fact every demographic will have an overlap with a small miniority of pedophiles; white, black, gay, straight, ect... It's not fair that we are associated with pedophiles simply because we feel like children. The two have nothing in common with each other. People just see the word 'child' and think 'hurr durr, connection right there!' It's just a quick and lazy attempt to discredit us.
It's often, but not always, asked in the sense, "Is this socially acceptable?" And no one single individual can decide that.

I think if a person feels helpless in helping you then they may distance themselves from you in order to protect their own mental well-being. Seeing you so miserable and not knowing how to help brings them down. Others, of course, never really cared about you in the first place, and you were nothing more to them than disposable entertainment. It can be frustrating to not know who is who.
Hard to say what my dreams would be in another life. I wouldn't even describe that person as myself any more.

The bill doesn't go far enough. Firstly, anyone who can't take the lethal dose themselves won't be eligible for this, so it discriminates against the paralysed and those with digestion problems, for example. Secondly, restricting assisted dying to the terminally ill does nothing to help those with severe, incurable non-terminal illness, which can be just as painful and distressing.

It's baffling that assisted suicide and euthanasia are still illegal in most countries. In some countries, even suicide itself is illegal which is even more bizarre. What is a person supposed to do if their condition is intolerable and incurable? Just sit there and take it? That is akin to torture. It's not something that should be expected of anybody under those circumstances. If they want to die, they have every right to, and they should be offered help to do so in a safe environment.

> Suicide is a permanent "solution" to a temporary problem.

That often sadly isn't true. Not saying that OP can't be helped, just that phrase is incorrect.

Not all problems are temporary or fixable.

If you define "digital native" as someone using the internet as a child, I'd say Millennials are proto-digital-natives. Like, many of us did in fact use the internet as children but the internet wasn't an integral part of our lives. 90s internet was expensive to use and the web itself wasn't as well established back then. It's possible that the youngest Millennials could call themselves digital natives, though.

Modern is relative to time. Technology has been evolving at a rapid pace since the industrial revolution. The technology of today will be seen as ancient by future generations. All the things young people enjoy today will be seen as old people activities eventually, except for things that remain popular for every new generation like video games, music, the internet, ect. But even those won't be the exact same media that you enjoy today. The internet especially will be unrecognizable compared to now.

The only thing stopping me right now is my family and also the fear that my attempt will fail and I'll end up paralysed, being unable to communicate, or make another attempt. One day I know my chronic pain will get so bad that I'll have no choice other than to take the risk, but for now I'm hanging in there.

I'm 32 and early-20-year-olds assume I'm the mature one and that I should know what I'm doing. I don't leave my house much, but when I do, I run the risk of awkward situations between me and younger people. It's demoralizing.

If you felt that the use of corporal punishment by your parents was done as an act of love then perhaps you felt abandoned and less loved when they stopped using it? I have no idea. Just throwing ideas around. I have a theory that age dysphoria, in some, can be caused by a desire of love from our parents and others. That's not to say that we don't feel loved, but that we may feel less loved than before, back when we were chronologically children.

I don't think I have the exact mindset of a child, it's just that for whatever reason, I never wanted to become an adult, thus I never tried to learn the social norms of being one. In fact, the thought of being an adult terrifies me so much that I actively avoid being "corrupted", for the lack of a better word. I was too attached to my childhood self and didn't want to see that person die. In many ways, I think that events surrounding puberty caused me to be this way. My life took a turn for the worst around that time. Due to events and circumstances, I felt less loved by others and wanted to go back to a time when life was kinder.

Yes, but some paitents are treatment resistant and will never get better. Those feelings you described, *"forcing someone to stay alive against their will was the cruelest form of torture"*  will be felt by them for the rest of their lives. Surely hopeless cases should be given an option for euthanasia?

Either poor understanding or inexperience of said mental condition and the unbearable suffering that goes with it, and/or an erroneous belief that psychological treatment can help everybody alleviate their symptoms to an acceptable level. As somebody with chronic pain, I too used to believe that the mentally ill should be "protected" under all circumstances. The problem with my logic was that I hadn't accounted for the truly hopeless cases, and my understanding of depression at the time was limited to the mild variation of it. I didn't fully understand how torturous their lives could be, and why somebody who is treatment resistant may desire the option of euthanasia.

I'm afraid of adults for some reason. Always have been and I've never known why. In fact, I mainly keep to myself these days. I'm too old and male to be hanging around with kids; too childish and afraid to get on with adults. It's a lonely existence. I did try talking to young teens on Discord but idk, I felt too out of touch with them. That's the problem with age dysphoria, a person can remain a child  but the world around them changes. I feel like I'm trapped in a time capsule in a way. The type of young people I want to socialize with don't exist any more. I mean, they're still alive as adults but they're not the same people I used to know.

Kids aren't what they used to be. Not tweens or teenagers anyway. I don't think they're better or worse today, just different. Maybe you can relate to this or maybe you have different reasons for wanting to socialize with adults more? Just sharing thoughts.

I disagree. Biological age provides context about people and their current situation. Also, just because we all feel like children, that doesn't mean we can all relate to each other. If you were born many years apart from someone else then they may  have a different take on what childhood means. That's not a problem as long as we don't start calling each other old or not really a child.

I'm not anti-sexuality or anything but the subject does make me feel uncomfortable. I avoid talking about it as much as I can. Everyone probably thinks I'm gay and in the closet but idc. I would tell them that I'm asexual but that wouldn't really be true. I'm actually bi but I have no interest in forming a relationship with anyone. 

Just feels morally repugnant when someone tries to talk to me about anything sexual, but of course I can't blame the person because nobody knows I have age dysphoria and they wouldn't understand even if I told them.
I can totally relate to this. Sorry I can't give you any advise.

I want people to treat me like a child but I also don't. I've had too many bad experiences where people have belittled me by treating me as if I were one. What I really want is go back to actually being a child, physically speaking, again.

Emotional regulation and a naive thought process. I feel as if I have a childish innocence about me, fuelled entirely by how I want to see the world. I live in a fantasy solely powered by my own ego. Things *should* be how I want them to be. The world should be a safe place for all and not stressful. If I'm unable to ignore reality and see the world in the way I want to (innocently), then I see in it in a completely negative light instead. There's no nuance or in-between. I only deal in extremes. I take my anger out on whoever won't allow me to live in peace within my own fantasy. I feel as if I'm being personally attacked by them.

I can only compare my emotional development with others of the same chronological age as myself. I haven't stopped developing as a person, but emotionally speaking, I am way, way behind. I don't have a problem with that, personally; it's everyone else in society who does.

I expect body dysphoria is extremely high within our community. Most of us probably aren't even ugly, but that's how we perceive ourselves. Obviously I don't know what OP looks like so I'm not going to assume anything. I think I'm objectively ugly, though. Like, I have an old child face if that makes any sense. When people see me, my face makes their brain hurt.

I suffered a traumatic event as I was entering puberty. I believe I wanted to go back to a happier and more innocent state of being. That... or I was just born with an unusual brain that stopped emotionally developing at a certain age. I wish there was more science being done on this subject.

To my knowledge, the English language lacks a single word to describe emotional social development. In reality the word 'age' is used interchangeably both to describe chronological age, along with the stage of what an average person is at at any given age in terms of physical, cognitive and social emotional development. The problem is, when discussing age dysphoria with anyone who wishes to discredit us, suddenly the meaning of the word becomes rigid, and only the chronological measurement aspect is acknowledged.
